input: Patch entry: flat FLRW Hubble–Schwarzschild correspondence, TIG-graded. Companion document: supplement/FLAT_FLRW_HUBBLE_SCHWARZSCHILD_CORRESPONDENCE.md (intended for Pallyman/Black_Hole_Cosmology).

metadata.title: Flat FLRW Hubble–Schwarzschild Correspondence
references: Pathria RK. The Universe as a Black Hole. Nature 240, 298-299 (1972)
Gibbons GW, Hawking SW. Cosmological event horizons, thermodynamics, and particle creation. Phys. Rev. D 15, 2738-2751 (1977)
changelog: 1.1.0 (2026-11-24): split CLM-HS-002 into 002A (ANCHORED ratio formula, Misner–Sharp mass) and 002B (OPEN HYPOTHESIS); CLM-HS-003 restated as null-expansion classification (super-Hubble = anti-trapped), framed as a constraint, not an impossibility.

derivation: Flat Friedmann: H^2 = (8 pi G/3) rho  =>  rho_c = 3H^2/(8 pi G)
Enclosed mass: M = (4 pi/3) rho_c R_H^3 = c^3/(2 G H)
Pure de Sitter special case: H^2 = Lambda c^2/3  =>  R_H = sqrt(3/Lambda)
Horizon entropy: S = k_B c^3 A/(4 G hbar), A = 4 pi R_H^2

claims.text: In any spatially flat FLRW universe at critical density rho_c = 3H^2/(8 pi G), the mass inside the Hubble sphere is M = c^3/(2GH), so its Schwarzschild radius 2GM/c^2 equals the Hubble radius c/H, at every epoch (matter, radiation or Lambda dominated).

For any sphere of areal radius R in spatially flat FLRW, the Misner–Sharp mass is M = H^2 R^3/(2G), so R_S/R = (R/R_H)^2 with R_H = c/H. Equal at R = R_H; R_S > R for super-Hubble spheres; R_S < R for sub-Hubble spheres.

Whether this correspondence identifies a physical black-hole interior, or can be embedded in a larger black-hole spacetime, depends on global geometry, causal structure and matching conditions. Not disproven; open research question (FLRW-interior / Schwarzschild-exterior matching models and collapse-bounce cosmologies exist).

Null-expansion classification: in expanding flat FLRW, outgoing light expands everywhere; ingoing light contracts inside R_H, is zero at R_H, and expands outside. Super-Hubble spheres are therefore ANTI-TRAPPED (both families expanding) — the white-hole-like / time-reversed structure — not future-trapped like a collapsing black hole (both contracting). In a contracting FLRW phase the signs reverse. This is a constraint any black-hole-universe model must explain (e.g. via collapse and bounce), not a prohibition on such models.
The Hubble radius is the apparent horizon of flat FLRW, not in general the cosmological event horizon; the two coincide only in pure de Sitter (R = sqrt(3/Lambda)).
Cosmological horizons carry area-law entropy S = k_B c^3 A/(4 G hbar), the same form as black-hole horizons, so equal areas imply equal information bounds.

Interpretations: the universe as a black-hole interior; the horizon as a holographic save state. Black-hole-interior cosmologies exist (e.g. Poplawski torsion bounce) but need extra physics; established holography (AdS/CFT) is for negative Lambda, ours is positive. The radius equality cannot discriminate these hypotheses; the JWST proper-time age-gradient predictions can.

ANCHORED: radius equality for any flat FLRW universe
R_S/R = (R/R_H)^2 (Misner–Sharp); super-Hubble spheres exceed their Schwarzschild expression
null-expansion classification: super-Hubble spheres anti-trapped in expanding FLRW
ISOMORPHIC: cosmological horizon <-> black-hole horizon in area and information capacity
ANALOGOUS: horizon as holographic save state / backup
OPEN_HYPOTHESIS: CLM-HS-002B: physical black-hole interior / embedding in larger black-hole spacetime

causal_validity.reason: Equality follows algebraically from the flat Friedmann equation; no causal claim beyond it.

scale_integrity.reason: Holds at every epoch of flat FLRW (matter, radiation, Lambda); physical-interpretation layer kept separate.

boundary_integrity.reason: Apparent horizon (c/H) explicitly distinguished from the event horizon; equal only in pure de Sitter.

measurement_integrity.reason: Derivation exact; observational test of the black-hole-interior hypothesis lives in the JWST age-gradient predictions, not here.

wave_function_coherence.reason: Inner (enclosed mass) and outer (horizon radius) quantities related exactly; interpretation argued.

substrate_sovereignty.reason: identity_claim_allowed false: a mass-radius correspondence is not identity with a trapped black-hole region.

corpus_completeness.reason: Primary references anchored; holography for positive Lambda left as an open research problem.

isomorphism_quality.note: 1.0 only where the claim is derived or anchored; interpretation layer graded separately.

mappings.target: Schwarzschild black hole of equal mass
residual_mismatches: expanding FLRW super-Hubble region is anti-trapped (both null expansions positive); a black-hole interior is future-trapped (both negative)
black-hole horizon is one surface about one center; Hubble horizon is observer-centered
Hubble radius is the apparent horizon, not generally the event horizon

outputs.public_translation: In any flat universe, the mass inside the Hubble sphere is exactly enough that its Schwarzschild radius equals the Hubble radius. This is a real, general result (Pathria 1972), and cosmological horizons carry the same area-law entropy as black holes (Gibbons & Hawking 1977). It does not by itself show that we live inside a black hole; that hypothesis is tested by its own predictions, such as the JWST age gradient.
outputs.uncertainty_statement: Black-hole-interior and holographic-backup interpretations are ANALOGOUS and untested by this derivation. Holography for positive Lambda remains open.
open_questions: Can flat FLRW be embedded in a larger black-hole spacetime with consistent matching conditions and no unphysical matter?
How does the boundary evolve as matter, radiation and dark energy change H?
Does the boundary area encode interior degrees of freedom in a physical holographic description (positive Lambda)?
Which observables differ from LambdaCDM? (candidate: JWST proper-time age gradient)
